The bar chart of annual sales of an electronics store in Nagpur shows these values:
Year | Sales (₹ lakh)
2020 | 40
2021 | 50
2022 | 45
2023 | 60
2024 | 75
What are the average annual sales over the five years?

The bar chart of annual sales of an electronics store in Nagpur shows these values:
Year | Sales (₹ lakh)
2020 | 40
2021 | 50
2022 | 45
2023 | 60
2024 | 75
By what percentage did sales increase from 2023 to 2024?
explanation: Increase = 75 − 60 = 15 lakh. Percentage increase = 15/60 × 100 = 25%. (Dividing by the 2024 value, 75, gives the wrong answer 20%.)
shortcut: Percentage change is always on the earlier (base) value

The bar chart of annual sales of an electronics store in Nagpur shows these values:
Year | Sales (₹ lakh)
2020 | 40
2021 | 50
2022 | 45
2023 | 60
2024 | 75
In which year was the percentage growth in sales over the previous year the highest?
explanation: Growth over the previous year: 2021: 10/40 = 25%; 2022: −5/50 = −10%; 2023: 15/45 ≈ 33.3%; 2024: 15/60 = 25%. The highest is 2023, even though the absolute increase in 2023 and 2024 is the same (15 lakh).
shortcut: Same absolute rise on a smaller base means a bigger percentage

Java | 120 | 150
Python | 200 | 240
Data Science | 80 | 140
Cloud | 100 | 110
By what percentage did the total enrolment increase from 2023 to 2024?

Students enrolled in four courses at a training institute in Pune:
Course | 2023 | 2024
Java | 120 | 150
Python | 200 | 240
Data Science | 80 | 140
Cloud | 100 | 110
The fee is ₹12,000 per student for Java and ₹15,000 per student for Data Science in both years. By how much did the combined fee collection from these two courses increase from 2023 to 2024?
explanation: Java: 150 − 120 = 30 more students × ₹12,000 = ₹3.6 lakh. Data Science: 140 − 80 = 60 more students × ₹15,000 = ₹9 lakh. Total increase = ₹3.6 lakh + ₹9 lakh = ₹12.6 lakh (₹26.4 lakh → ₹39 lakh).
shortcut: Multiply each course's change in students by its own fee

stem:
A pie chart shows how the Iyer family splits its total monthly expenditure of ₹60,000:
Item | Share of expenditure (%)
Rent | 30
Food | 25
Education | 15
Transport | 10
Others | 20
What is the central angle of the sector for Education in the pie chart?
explanation: Central angle = share × 360° = 15/100 × 360° = 54°. (Education spending itself is 15% of ₹60,000 = ₹9,000.)

stem:
A pie chart shows how the Iyer family splits its total monthly expenditure of ₹60,000:
Item | Share of expenditure (%)
Rent | 30
Food | 25
Education | 15
Transport | 10
Others | 20
If the family's spending on Food rises by 50% while every other amount stays the same, what will Food's share of the new total expenditure be?
explanation: Food = 25% of ₹60,000 = ₹15,000; after a 50% rise it is ₹22,500. The new total = ₹60,000 + ₹7,500 = ₹67,500. Food's share = 22,500/67,500 = 1/3 = 33⅓%. (37.5% wrongly ignores the change in the total.)
shortcut: Recompute the total before taking the new share
